This is a quick and easy way to establish group relationships and adds quite a bit of interest to the standard group. I never was much for the 'you all meet in a tavern' or everyone 'happens to know each other first'.

Its an easy system where you take turns using dice from a pool to make choices off tables to for connections with people to either side of you. As the turns go around the table you are given the choice to add another connection or further define and existing connection.

sample: from Dragon Slayers(Logan Bonner)

relationships...

1 Family and Romance

1 Siblings 2 Parent / child who was raised by others 3 Unrequited lovers 4 Spouses in an arranged marriage 5 Linked by blood ritual 6 Orphan / caretaker

2 Adventure

1 Assassin / target 2 Rescuer / rescuee 3 Employer / henchman 4 Former cellmates 5 Master / defeated foe turned into servant 6 Bounty hunter / bounty

3 Magic

1 Creator / golem 2 Master / thrall 3 Sorcerer / apprentice 4 Diabolist / intended sacrificial victim 5 Simulacrum / real person 6 Werewolf in human form / werewolf in wolf for

4 Culture

1 Same non-human race (elf, dwarf, etc.) 2 Tribemates 3 Worshipers of the same god 4 Bound by a blood ritual 5 Outcasts 6 Members of the same guild

5 Fellowship

1 Longtime adventuring companions 2 Drinking buddies 3 Reluctant allies 4 New blood / veteran adventurer 5 Leader / wannabe leader 6 Vicious scoundrel / pacifist healer

6 War

1 Same battalion 2 Mercenaries 3 Fought for different sides 4 You each have a scar the other gave you 5 Fighter / coward 6 “You killed my father”

Just to give you an idea if the initial pool of dice rolled had a 1 and a 6 on my first choice i could choose family and romance with someone and my next choice would define it as either I orphaned them or they orphaned me.

I feel it gives the groups a more 'organic' feel rather than the just throw everyone together and expect them to all be pals. Not necessarily a plug for the game but you can buy it for $12 US online, more that it is a unique way of defining character relations that I hadn't seen before.
